children.text: oṃ śāstrāṇy adhītya medhāvī abhyasya ca punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>. Having studied the scriptures, an intelligent person, and having practiced again and again,
should, after knowing supreme <s>Brahman</s>, then cast them away like a firebrand.

children.text: oṃkāraṃ ratham āruhya viṣṇuṃ kṛtvā tu sārathim
children.translated_text: Having mounted <s>Oṃkāra</s> (the syllable Oṃ) as a chariot and made <s>Viṣṇu</s> the charioteer,
the seeker of the station of <s>Brahmaloka</s>, wholly intent upon the worship of <s>Rudra</s>,

children.text: tāvad rathena gantavyaṃ yāvad rathapathi sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: should travel by the chariot for as long as he remains upon the chariot-road.
After crossing the chariot-road, he abandons the chariot and proceeds.
Having left behind the <s>mātrā</s> (mora), the sign, and the word, one is free from sound and articulation;

children.text: asvareṇa makāreṇa padaṃ sūkṣmaṃ ca gacchati ||
children.translated_text: by means of the soundless letter <s>ma</s>, one reaches the subtle state.
The five objects beginning with sound, and the mind itself, are exceedingly restless.

children.text: cintayed ātmano raśmīn pratyāhāraḥ sa ucyate ||
children.translated_text: One should contemplate them as rays of the Self; that is called <s>pratyāhāra</s> (withdrawal of the senses).

children.text: tarkaś caiva samādhiś ca ṣaḍaṅgo yoga ucyate ||
children.translated_text: reasoning, and absorption—these are called the six-limbed yoga.
Just as the impurities of ores from mountains are burned away by the blowing of a furnace,
so the faults produced by the senses are burned away through restraint of the breath.

children.text: prāṇāyāmair dahed doṣān dhāraṇābhiś ca kilbiṣam
children.translated_text: Through breath controls one should burn away faults, and through concentrations, sin.
